title: Family and first instruments: heel bass, comb, mandolin
summary: His father was a farmer and steamboat cook; all five brothers played music. He started with a comb and heel-bass, then learned mandolin by listening to his cousin and brother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, my father didn't play any music. He was a farmer. He used to fire and cook on a steamboat, you know.
Was that on a bayou out there?

Yeah, by the push. And I had five brothers of us. We all played music. Were you the oldest? No, no. I had two older than me and two younger than me. My youngest brother is still now in California. He played saxophone and kindly. He's a wonderful musician. Yeah. And I also played saxophone.
Can you tell us about the first instrument that you took up? What did you start on?
The first instrument that I took up was my heel. Just a bit of something you took? And then a head comb. A comb? Yeah, a comb. Paper? Yeah, with paper. See?
Did it stomp your heel too?
No, I rubbed my heel on the, you know, and made base. Oh, yeah? Oh, I see.

No, on the floor. On the floor? Yeah, on the floor. Yeah, it was fine. And after that, my cousin and my brother used to play mandolin and guitar, you know? And by listening to them, I just liked myself, you know, just by listening. So I learned how to play mandolin and my first song that I played was Home Sweet Home and I was hitting a note every five minutes, you know, and my sister called me to go get a bucket of water from the well. So I said, we used to call it Chook, the nickname, you know? And I said, yeah, I said, yeah, there's a dime. I said, go ahead. I didn't want to stop, you see? I just continued trying to play Home Sweet Home. So that goes on for a good while, about a couple of months. So I began to play Home Sweet Home. And the band leader, Joe Gabriel, who was my band leader, but that was his instrument I was playing on, you know? He played mandolin and violin. So I didn't want him to catch me playing on his instrument because I didn't know whether he was like it or not.
